title: Finite free transport of regular quotient completion units
statement: Let $R\to S$ be a map of commutative ring sheaves on a small site. Fix an $R$-module basis isomorphism $R^{\oplus d}\cong S$, $d\geq0$, and a global section $a$ of $R$ whose multiplication on both $R$ and $S$ is injective. Assume countable products in both module-sheaf categories are exact. For a K-flat complex $P$ [def-pc-kflat-complex] with flat terms over $R$ (tensoring with each term is exact), put $Q=P\otimes_R S$, which computes derived change of rings [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. For $T=R,S$ and $H=P,Q$ respectively, let $C_{T,a}(H)$ be the product cone of $H\otimes_T T/a^nT$ with its zero shifted-component quotient unit $\eta_{T,a,H}$ [lem-pur-regular-quotient-completion-unit]. Restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars] identifies $Q$ with $P^{\oplus d}$, identifies $C_{S,a}(Q)$ with $C_{R,a}(P)^{\oplus d}$, and under these identifications sends $\eta_{S,a,Q}$ to $\eta_{R,a,P}^{\oplus d}$. Consequently, if $P$ is locally derived $(a)$-complete in the local derived-Hom sense of [lem-pur-regular-quotient-completion-unit], then $Q$ is locally derived $(a)$-complete as an $S$-object. All tensor products of module sheaves are sheafified tensor products [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], applied termwise to complexes when an ordinary tensor is written.

source.place: Lemma 3.4.12, pp. 22-23; finite direct-sum calculation of the quotient-tower units, written here as a general ringed-site argument.

proof.text: Write $U$ for restriction from $S$ to $R$. By the module-sheaf limits and colimits theorem, kernels, cokernels and products have the same underlying abelian sheaves for either coefficient ring. Thus $U$ is exact, preserves products and finite sums, and commutes with cohomology. It reflects zero cohomology sheaves because it leaves the underlying abelian sheaf unchanged. Consequently a chain map of $S$-modules is a quasi-isomorphism if its restriction is one. The theorem applies on this small site, where abelian sheafification exists; there is no need to assume enough points.

source.place: Tags 03DA (lemma-abelian) and 03DB (lemma-limits-colimits): exact forgetful functor and underlying limits/colimits.

proof.text: Apply lem-pur-finite-free-scalar-extension to construct the normalized scalar-extension isomorphism α. Apply lem-pur-finite-free-quotient-tower to this α to obtain the strict quotient-tower isomorphism τ. Evaluate τ and use the finite-product comparison to define θ_n; its normalization is exactly the quotient square required here. These steps need no regularity or derived-category hypothesis.

Apply lem-pur-finite-power-roos-comparison to the additive, countable-product-preserving restriction functor U and the strict isomorphism τ. Its two coordinate formulas, followed by the evaluation product identity for θ_n, give both specified block formulas for β.

The regular quotient unit has zero shifted block and quotient augmentation in the other block, by the explicit Roos augmentation formula and koszulRepresentativeAugmentation_quotient. Project the claimed unit square to finite factor i, both Roos blocks, and tower level n. The first block is zero on both sides. The second is the quotient square for θ_n. The two blocks and all their product projections jointly detect equality of chain maps, proving the unit square in the displayed complexes.

Suppose $P$ is locally derived $(a)$-complete as in the hypothesis. Apply the regular quotient completion-unit criterion with coefficient ring $R$: $P$ is K-flat, multiplication by $a$ on $R$ is injective, and countable products of $R$-modules are exact, exactly as required. It makes $\eta_{R,a,P}$ an isomorphism in $D(R)$, hence a quasi-isomorphism of the displayed complexes. A finite direct sum of this map is a quasi-isomorphism: kernels and images of its differentials are the coordinatewise finite sums, so its $k$-th cohomology map is $H^k(\eta_{R,a,P})^{\oplus d}$. The identity in step 4 and the chain isomorphisms $\alpha,\beta$ make $U(\eta_{S,a,Q})$ a quasi-isomorphism. Step 1 then makes $\eta_{S,a,Q}$ a quasi-isomorphism over $S$. This includes $d=0$, where both complexes are zero.

source.place: Lemma 3.4.12, natural-map criterion, instantiated by lem-pur-regular-quotient-completion-unit; finite coordinatewise cohomology calculation.

proof.text: K-flat change of rings with flat terms gives K-flatness of the displayed termwise extension Q. The regular quotient completion-unit criterion over S applies to Q, the given regular image of a, and exact countable products. The quasi-isomorphism of its prescribed unit obtained above therefore implies local derived principal completeness over S. No derived comparison is needed: the conclusion already names this concrete Q.

proof_origin.place: Bhatt--Scholze Lemma 3.4.12, pp. 22-23; explicit normalized basis/quotient-system comparison and two-block Roos transport. Completion follows by finite products of quasi-isomorphisms and reflection under exact restriction.
